independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Theorem 4.3's literal second sentence assumes distinct centers, whereas the adjacent Theorem 4.2 explicitly assumes partial optimality. The report acknowledges that interpreting 'solution' as a partial optimum avoids the defect and confines the claim to the literal statement.
independent_check.decisive_check: Freshly recomputed means of {-5,0,2} and {-2,1,4} as -1 and 1, with costs 26 and 18. At these fixed centers, 2 must move from first to second and -2 from second to first; 0 alone ties, and all other nearest labels are strict. Thus the two minimizing assignments have distances 2 or 3 from the supplied P, while T(P) permits exactly one move. Data are all distinct, N>K, positive weights, and phi=x^2 is strictly convex on R.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: Adding P in A(C) makes any one tied reassignment preserve fixed-center minimum. Distinct centers imply the tied point is neither center; the nonnegative Bregman center-shift terms then give strict decrease. Lemma D.4 supplies precisely this partial-optimality premise at the main invocation, so the core convergence theorem is not refuted. Minor literal-statement qualification, not a general theorem-collapse claim.
independent_check.result: Supported with the already explicit alternative interpretation and bounded repair.

independent_check.source_and_assumptions: Fresh static reading confirms constructors retain supplied ordering; rand initialization can repeat centers; both empty-cluster repairs test donor mass but omit x_g != c_b; the first tie is assigned to index 1 even if already there. Original Algorithm 1 samples without replacement and excludes moving a point equal to donor center.
independent_check.decisive_check: Independently traced X=(0,-1,1), unit weights, centers(0,0): every nearest label is 0; first empty repair moves the ordered point0 to label1, giving (1,0,0) with both means0. On the next pass the same repaired labels equal the old labels; first tie handling sets label1 again and exits unchanged. Cost is 2. Moving alpha mass of -1 gives sums +alpha and -alpha, masses 2-alpha and 1+alpha; total within-cluster squared cost is 2-alpha^2/(2-alpha)-alpha^2/(1+alpha), strictly less for every positive alpha and 1/2 at alpha=1. Centers also approach the returned centers as alpha goes to zero, establishing non-CJ-local as well.
independent_check.alternatives_and_scope: The theoretical repair rule excludes this exact trace, and the real-world driver's sorted deduplication changes its order. The report therefore treats the later release as a separate, Minor implementation defect with historical effect unresolved. Aligning the rules addresses this mechanism; no general finite-precision guarantee is certified.
independent_check.result: Supported static counterexample; no author-code execution.
